newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Axe-wielding burglar robs neighbour of HK's Tung.
newsitem.headline: Axe-wielding burglar robs neighbour of HK's Tung.

text.p: A burglar armed with an axe broke into a house next door to a residence of Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's future leader, and wounded a housemaid, police said on Wednesday.
The man, aged about 30, entered the house in the chic Deep Water Bay area in the early hours of Wednesday, threatened the woman and stole HK$100 (US$13) from her, a police spokesman told Reuters.

The 54-year-old maid, who had been alone in the house, was treated in hospital with minor head and arm injuries after struggling with the intruder, he said. Police declined to say if she had suffered axe wounds. The man was still on the run.
A spokesman for the territory's future chief executive said the burgled house stands next to the home where Tung breakfasted with visiting U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich in March.
The former shipping magnate takes office on July 1 when Hong Kong reverts to China after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

Tung's residence is heavily guarded by the Hong Kong VIP Protection Unit, the territory's equivalent of the U.S. Secret Service, and there were no immediate plans to tighten security, the spokesman said.
